per_option_rationale.rationale: Adds 6 to 30 as if differences grow by a constant of 0 (constant differences), giving 36.
Identifies the rule as n(n+1) but computes 6 x 7 = 40 by using n=6 instead of n=6 correctly (which is 42), a position-counting slip.
Adds 16 (double the previous difference of 10 minus 4) to 30 = 46, misidentifying the second-level difference rule.

explanation: The series is n(n+1) for n = 1, 2, 3, ...: 1x2=2, 2x3=6, 3x4=12, 4x5=20, 5x6=30, 6x7=42, 7x8=56. The missing 6th term is 6 x 7 = 42.

explanation_sections.punchline: Each term is the product of two consecutive integers n and n+1; position 6 gives 6 x 7 = 42.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: check products of consecutive integers: 1x2=2, 2x3=6, 3x4=12, 4x5=20, 5x6=30. Pattern confirmed at n(n+1). Position 6: 6x7=42. Verify position 7: 7x8=56.
explanation_sections.lesson: The oblong number series n(n+1) has differences 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, ... - even numbers. If differences are even and grow by 2, test n(n+1).
explanation_sections.timing: 40-50 seconds. Verify with the term after the gap (7x8=56 matches) to confirm.
